description: Hand-written earlier session in this repository (synthetic: the requests, thoughts, and answers were written for receipts-bench; every tool output was captured by running the step on the starting repository). The session is about behavior that the task does not change, and none of it hints at the task.

episodes.request: The department head asked how the class summary at the bottom of the report is worked out: what do the mean and the median cover, and which letters are listed? No changes please.

steps.thought: The statistics are in their own module.
The report module shows how the summary is printed.
The statistics tests show the edge cases.

finish.thought: stats.ts, report.ts and the tests cover the whole summary.
finish.report: The summary comes after the student table and an empty line, in four lines. 'students: N' is the number of students in the report. 'mean:' and 'median:' are the mean and the median of the students' final percentages, printed with one decimal place by formatPercent; mean and median in src/stats.ts return 0 for an empty list, and the median of an even number of students is the average of the two middle values. 'letters:' lists how many students got each letter, best letter first, as 'A 2, B+ 1'; letterCounts leaves out letters that nobody got, and the line shows '-' when there are no students. All four lines use the same final percentages as the table, so the summary always agrees with the lines above it. test/stats.test.ts checks the mean of a short list and of an empty one, the median of an odd and of an even number of values, and that the letter counts list the best letter first and skip letters nobody got.

finish.report: examples/scores.csv has 21 score rows after its header: 7 each for the students s01, s02 and s03. By category there are 6 homework rows, 6 quiz rows, 6 exam rows and 3 project rows, so each student has two homework assignments, two quizzes, two exams and one project. (The lines with count 1, student and category, are the header.)

episodes.request: Which npm scripts does the project have, and which Node version does it need?

steps.thought: package.json has the scripts and the engines field.
The TypeScript settings matter for running the code directly.

finish.report: package.json defines two scripts. npm test runs node --experimental-strip-types --test with the spec reporter on test/*.test.ts, one test file at a time (--test-concurrency=1). npm run report -- FILE runs bin/gradebook.ts report FILE with type stripping. The engines field asks for Node 22.6 or later, the first version with --experimental-strip-types, and there are no dependencies at all. tsconfig.json is only for editors and type checking (noEmit): it allows .ts import extensions and only erasable syntax, which is what lets Node run the files as they are.

episodes.request: Last question: how many tests are there for the report, the statistics, the CSV parsing, and the command line?

steps.thought: Count the top-level tests in those four files.

finish.thought: The counts are in the output.
finish.report: 19 tests: 3 in test/report.test.ts, 4 in test/stats.test.ts, 8 in test/scores.test.ts and 4 in test/cli.test.ts. Every test is a top-level test() call from node:test, so the spec reporter lists each of them once.
